Jessica refuses to believe that the editor of her latest book has committed suicide and is determined to find out the truth.
Infrared cameras seem to prove Jessica's writing student is guilty of killing his abusive stepfather.
The closing of a family-owned department store leads to a double murder in New York, and Jessica has no shortage of suspects in the crime.
Fresh blood stains indicate foul play when Seth (William Windom) disappears; a proliferation of strangers in town raises Jessica's suspicions.
A Texas trucker (Earl Holliman) is charged with insurance fraud; his son (Patrick Cassidy) is accused of murder.
Jessica searches for a motive when a legendary maestro, who is about to lose control of his protégé, is found murdered.
Burglaries and a murder occur when the carnival comes to Cabot Cove but doesn't seem to bring in a great deal of money.
Jessica's probe of a friend's kidnapping in Amsterdam leads to two murders and a diamond-smuggling ring.
Internal strife at an earthquake-shaken California zoo culminates in an employee's death from snake bite.
Jessica's discovery that Cabot Cove's Revolutionary War hero was actually a traitor results in a TV director's murder.
Jessica's vacation to Honolulu becomes chaotic when the son of her host, power broker Matt Kinkaid, vanishes during a hotly contested U.S. Senate election.
Jessica investigates when, during a visit to San Francisco, an advice columnist (Eileen Brennan) falls victim to a crazed gunman.
Accidentally tapped into a closed-circuit video surveillance system, Jessica's neighbor witnesses scheming, a robbery and then a murder.
While vacationing in Martinique, Jessica is called on to help an acquaintance (Wayne Rogers) accused of a woman's (Cassie Yates) murder.
The mysterious deaths of a winery matriarch's son and a rival vintner lead Jessica into a world of greed and betrayal.
Jessica seeks a link between the electrocution of the town bully and the hanging of a teacher who was his lover.

While working on an infomercial, Jessica helps a detective friend (George DiCenzo) probe a strangulation, and tries to find out why a member of her studio audience (Gale Hansen) is found dead during the taping.
Jessica helps a Russian police officer (David Ogden Stiers) capture the elusive mastermind behind the theft of a Fabergé egg.
The pervasive stench of death looms over Jessica and Seth's visit to his cousin's South Carolina plantation.
Jessica takes a trip to Egypt to finalize a cultural exchange program and ends up searching for a killer and a stolen artifact.
A stalker threatens a gifted soprano (Khrystyne Haje) about to make her debut, and Jessica steps in to help with the investigation.
Carrie falls into a deep mine while chasing a butterfly; a drunken former miner must get his act together to rescue her.
After witnessing a loud argument, Laura is under the impression that Mr. Oleson kills his wife, but no one believes her.
Charles rushes back to Wisconsin after he learns his mother has died, and his father is suicidal with grief.
Charles' father stays with the Ingalls, but an incident with Laura deepens his depression.
Laura struggles to understand why the rest of her family does not like her goat, which she saves from farmer Parson's shotgun.
Charles tries to tolerate three bullies, until they assault his family.
Laura asks help from a blind recluse (Burl Ives) and his trapper son (Johnny Crawford) when Charles has a hunting accident.
The community's children are trapped by a sudden snowstorm while on their way home from school. With Michael Landon and Karen Grassle.
Mr. Edwards' adopted son John decides to refuse a college scholarship when Mary agrees to get married to him.
When Mr. Edwards takes his deathly ill daughter to a mountain cabin to nurse her, Laura tries to help.
Mrs. Oleson casts Nellie as the lead in the children's play; a girl plots marriage for her widowed mother.
The Ingalls try to help a boy who is rejected by the townsfolk because his father is an Indian warrior.
Mary (Melissa Sue Anderson) needs an immediate operation, so Charles (Michael Landon) leaves the farm for a dangerous high-paying job.

A black boy (guest star Todd Bridges) enslaves himself to the Ingallses in exchange for an education. With Michael Landon and Karen Grassle.
Nightmares plague Laura (Melissa Gilbert) after she steals a small toy. With Michael Landon, Karen Grassle and Melissa Sue Anderson.
The boys want to prove that a slow-witted classmate can beat Mary and Nellie for class president.
When heavy rains make it impossible to plant their crops, the Ingalls and Edwards families head west to search for gold.
Charles (Michael Landon) regrets uprooting his family to the camps until he gets gold fever. With Karen Grassle, Melissa Sue Anderson and Melissa Gilbert.
A lonely elderly woman tries to settle in Walnut Grove. With Michael Landon, Karen Grassle, Melissa Sue Anderson and Melissa Gilbert.
Charles and Mary (Michael Landon, Melissa Sue Anderson) take their first trip to Chicago. With Karen Grassle and Melissa Gilbert.
Tragedy strikes after Laura (Melissa Gilbert) convinces a mother to let her daughter go swimming in the creek. With Michael Landon and Karen Grassle.
Gossip flies about Caroline and a man (Gil Gerard) building her kitchen in exchange for room and board.
A pack of wild dogs, crazed with hunger, kills the livestock of Walnut Grove farmers. With Michael Landon, Karen Grassle, Melissa Sue Anderson and Melissa Gilbert.
After an unknown thief plagues Walnut Grove, Laura (Melissa Gilbert) and her friend investigate. With Michael Landon and Karen Grassle.
Doc Baker (Kevin Hagen) decides to retire after a patient dies. With Michael Landon, Karen Grassle, Melissa Sue Anderson and Melissa Gilbert.
Mary (Melissa Sue Anderson) is held hostage by the outlaw Jesse James (guest star Dennis Rucker). With Michael Landon, Karen Grassle and Melissa Gilbert.
Jonathan Garvey's barn burns down leaving the family with no means of support, but Jonathan is angry when his wife takes a job at the post office.
Charles take Jonathan's place in a bout with an aging fighter (Moses Gunn), but victory dims when Charles realizes the boxer is badly injured.
Mary plans to meet a shy suitor at the Mankato Fair, until she encounters his charming balloonist boss.

An American Indian boy arrives in town seeking medical help for his ailing father. With Michael Landon and Karen Grassle.
Laura wants to impress a newly discovered old buddy; Charles and Jonathan try to start a freight line, which leads them further away from home.

The saga in the Berkshires continues with round two of Bethenny versus Luann; Jules adjusts to life without a nanny; the women attend Ramona's holiday party, during which Ramona encourages Luann to apologize to Carole.

In Vermont, Siggy and Dolores comfort Jacqueline who is licking her wounds; Teresa and Melissa don't understand why Jacqueline is playing the victim, prompting Jacqueline to lose her cool and say things she'll never be able to take back.

Social edition; Teresa struggles with the loss of her mother, and her friends plan a weekend getaway to Boca Raton, Fla.; Siggy introduces Margaret Josephs to the group; tensions flare when Danielle Staub makes her return.

Siggy and Dolores refuse to attend Margaret's launch party; Teresa begins to work on a new book.
Danielle shares a secret with Teresa that could destroy Teresa's friendship with Dolores.
Lisa Vanderpump visits a sex shop while looking for space for a new restaurant.

Kyle and Lisa Vanderpump undergo cryotherapy; Erika invites the others to watch her perform.

The women have brunch at Kathryn and Donnie's San Diego home; Eileen gets an Erika Jayne makeover; Kyle meets an old friend who has advice about dealing with sister Kim; Munchausen's syndrome casts a dark cloud over Erika's pool party.

Claudia decides to give stand-up comedy a whirl but soon realizes she's in over her head; NeNe brings the women together for an evening of therapy with Dr. Jeff, but NeNe storms out of the session leaving everyone else puzzled.

Dr. Jeff leads the women to a breakthrough; NeNe studies for her Broadway debut; Kenya's cast reads her script for the first time; Phaedra meets with an attorney; Claudia continues to encourage the women to form better friendships.

Instead of going to the Philippines with the others, NeNe chooses to work on her upcoming role in a Broadway production; Phaedra opens up to Claudia; the group is imbued with feelings of positivity and peace that last until dinner time.

In the Philippines, the women visit Manila and a volcano, then they go on a shopping excursion followed by a pajama party; Phaedra and Kenya have an emotionally charged discussion; NeNe is overcome during a costume fitting in New York.
Kenya shoots her TV pilot; Cynthia strives to perfect her accent for a role; Todd drops a bomb.
Bethenny experiences a health scare; the women attend a high-society dog wedding.
Carole and her friend, Heather Thomson, go ice skating; Bethenny receives surprising health news.
Luann confronts Ramona, while Sonja shares news about her relationship with Luann's boyfriend.
Jules gives Bethenny a piece of her mind; Sonja hosts a dinner party; the women head to Mohegan Sun.
The women are in good spirits at the casino as the dining, dancing and gambling gets underway.
The women decide to vacation in Miami; Bethenny reveals information about Luann and Tom.
Melissa and Teresa get into a huge fight, threatening the progress of the restaurant.

Teresa takes her daughters and her father on vacation to Puerto Rico, but the fun quickly turns into family turmoil; Margaret and Dolores face off; Siggy gets hormone therapy; Melissa and Joe argue over how to parent Antonia.

As Teresa and Dolores try to repair their fragile friendship, Dolores drops a bomb on Teresa regarding Danielle; Siggy hosts a Women's Empowerment Retreat; Margaret and Melissa worry they will feel the wrath of Siggy again.

While at Siggy's retreat, Margaret opens up about her relationship with her step-children, and Teresa talks about her resentment toward Joe; Melissa and Margaret plan a fun surprise; Siggy and Dolores confront Teresa about a rumor.

Teresa, Melissa, Margaret, and Danielle square off with Dolores, Siggy and Kim D. at the annual Posche Fashion Show; Teresa confronts Kim D. face to face about the cheating rumors; the women wonder whether they should go to Italy together.
Trying to fix their fractured friendships, the women take a trip to Milan, but rising tensions lead to an explosive fight that may divide them forever; back in New Jersey, Joe hosts a guys night.
Will, Jack and Karen try and rouse a devastated and bedridden Grace after she loses her boyfriend, Nathan.
Will and Grace back different candidates for the upcoming mayoral election.
Will, Grace, Jack and Karen make a day of it as they head to Thanksgiving get-togethers at the houses of their respective families.
At the gym, Will sees a man (Patrick Breen) who seems familiar, while Jack tries to popularize a new saying.
Grace is hired to decorate the windows at Barney's; Will meets a ballet dancer and is too embarrassed to introduce his friends.
Grace schemes to hook up the mistress (Lesley Ann Warren) of Will's father with another man in order to break up the relationship.
After rediscovering a handsome high-school friend who's doing time, Grace dreams of their life together outside the Big House.
Grace reveals her ex-boyfriend's faults to his bride at the wedding rehearsal; Elliot's mother (Rosie O'Donnell) demands that Jack never see him again.
Jack uses Grace as bait to expose a rival (Matt Damon) as heterosexual in order to secure a spot in a gay men's chorus.
Will and Grace try to find more expansive digs despite the efforts of Sandra Bernhard; Jack stumbles across Karen's lowlife mother (guest star Suzanne Pleshette).
Moving into their new dream apartment makes Will and Grace homesick; Jack tries to reconcile Karen with her grifter mom (guest star Suzanne Pleshette).
Will presents his newly reconciled parents (Sydney Pollack, Blythe Danner) with a cruise for their anniversary, but their individual secrets ruin his hopes.
Will salvages a cherished garden gnome in the aftermath of his parent's divorce; Jack's afraid of being typecast as a straight man.
When Jack works instead of taking his son to a basketball tournament, he learns from Will that he missed his son's first kiss with a girl.
When the bride-to-be gets sick, Will persuades Grace to help plan the wedding for his visiting friends.
A detective (Michael Douglas) helps Will search for his stolen computer; a crazy neighbor (Molly Shannon) opens a business and prospers by stealing Grace's ideas.
Will takes Grace to have her picture taken after he wins a sitting with an eccentric celebrity photographer.
Will wants Grace to be the mother of his baby; Jack and Karen are inspired to pursue their own goals.
Will and Grace vacillate on artificial or natural means of conceiving a baby; Jack receives career advice from his show-business idol, Cher.
A dashing doctor (Harry Connick Jr.) on horseback rescues Grace; Karen debates cheating on her imprisoned husband with hot-blooded suitor Lionel (Rip Torn).

Stalking Kevin Bacon (guest starring as himself) pays off for Jack when he is hired as the actor's personal assistant; Will and Grace pursue parenthood. Harry Connick Jr. and Rip Torn also guest star.
Smitten with the handsome doctor (Harry Connick Jr.), Grace stalls for time to reconsider having a baby with Will.
Karen and Jack hatch a plan to end Will and Grace's ongoing feud by tricking them into attending the same child's birthday party.
Leo (guest star Harry Connick Jr.) drags Grace on a scary cycling trip in the autumn countryside. Jason Marsden also guest stars.
Will's aggressive new boss (Gene Wilder) orders him to fire his friend; Grace and Jack discover Karen is living out of her limousine.
Grace uses indecorous language when meeting Leo's parents; Jack's acting coach (Eileen Brennan) disparages his meager talent.
Grace begins to have cold feet as her relatives start arriving for her wedding, while Will tries to overcome his mixed emotions.
Will is uneasy about the whole idea of Grace marrying Leo (guest star Harry Connick Jr.). Debbie Reynolds and Katie Couric also guest star.
Will invites Karen to move in with him after she is kicked out of the Plaza Hotel; Elton John is an all-seeing arbiter of gay style.
Grace has only two tickets to "The Nutcracker" and cannot decide whether to take Will or Leo. Mary McDonough guest stars.
Jack convinces Will to join a gay soccer team; Karen is giddy in anticipation of her date with a handsome restaurateur (Andy Garcia).
Grace is puzzled by her new neighbor -- a bizarre bohemian woman.
Will and Jack coach Karen's cousin (Dan Futterman) on his new gay lifestyle, reminding Will of his own experience of coming out in 1986.
Karen's rival (Minnie Driver) attempts to manipulate Jack; Will and Grace revitalize their friendship with a night of board games.
Jack encounters his former babysitter (guest star Demi Moore) and lapses into childlike behavior. Rosanna Arquette and Leigh-Allyn Baker also guest star.
Will and Jack's transformation of Karen's cousin Barry is complete; Karen duels with Beverly during a silent auction for charity.
Jealous Will spots Barry (Dan Futterman) disappearing with Jack; Karen trades places with Rosario to woo a handsome handyman (Bruno Campos).
Will forms an anti-romance club with Karen and his boss (Gene Wilder).
Will attempts to surprise Grace for her birthday by sneaking Leo back from Africa; Jack and Karen take their mission to keep Leo's return secret too seriously.
Karen's search for a roommate leads to a high-maintenance individual, who shares many of her eccentricities; Grace and Jack intervene when Will uses painkillers as a crutch.
Karen hires a somewhat immature divorce attorney (guest star Macaulay Culkin) to oppose Will in court.
When Karen's ex-husband dies, she and her British rival (Minnie Driver) have a contest of wills; Leo (Harry Connick Jr.) is needed in Guatemala.
Karen confronts her ex-husband's mistress before inviting everybody for a ceremony on her yacht; Grace suffers from jealousy after meeting her husband's sexy co-worker.
Will and Jack awake in a precarious position while at sea; Grace discovers love letters in Leo's bag from a female colleague.
Grace is vexed when she learns that Leo's ex-girlfriend (Mira Sorvino) is intimately acquainted with Will.
Karen invites Grace and Leo to play tennis at her exclusive club, but her fierce playing style drives Grace away.
Jack lands a speaking role opposite James Earl Jones in an off-Broadway play and gives the veteran actor some pointers.
Will takes Leo on shopping sprees and for high tea to help him rekindle his love of the city; Karen coaches Jack for the annual gay spelling bee.
Will takes his mother for an afternoon stroll and bumps into an attractive bachelor (Dylan McDermott); Karen continues her lifelong quest to hunt down hubby-stealing Lorraine.
An unorthodox doctor (Jack Black) gives Karen her annual physical; Jack begs Will to support his decision to become a student nurse.
Will urges Grace to stay in New York so they can spend some time together; Karen strong-arms Jack's nursing teacher into letting him skip class but still make the grade.
Will catches the eye of a female diner after being stood up; Grace bumps into a man (Tom Everett Scott) with whom she once shared a forgettable encounter; Karen runs into her nemesis, Candice Bergen.

A weak bladder forces Will to entrust Grace with his place in line for Barry Manilow tickets; Grace's mother (Debbie Reynolds) cancels their annual mother-daughter shopping trip to have dinner with Jack.

Grace's freeloading sister (Geena Davis) comes to town to launch her latest business enterprise; Karen spurns Lyle (John Cleese), then changes her mind after Lorraine (Minnie Driver) expresses her disapproval.
A rich plastic surgeon (guest star Hal Linden) tries to buy Will's affection; Grace boycotts a new restaurant.
Will's new client (Dave Foley) falls for Jack; Grace and Karen discover hidden money while trying to fix the plumbing in Leo's cabin.
Will is the only single man in a cooking class full of couples, including Jack and his new boyfriend (Dave Foley); Karen's mother (Suzanne Pleshette) asks Grace to decorate her apartment.
Will and Grace begin a business venture selling apartments; Jack runs into his former acting mentor, Zandra; Karen and Lyle (John Cleese) try to renew romance.
Will and Grace try to break up Jack and Stuart (Dave Foley) so they can sell the apartment for a higher price; Karen demands that Lyle (John Cleese) discipline his daughter (Minnie Driver).
Real estate entrepreneurs Will and Grace face formidable competition on the East Side from a lesbian couple (Edie Falco, Chloë Sevigny); John Edward gives Karen some psychic guidance.
Jack and Grace stumble upon Stuart (Dave Foley) watching a movie matinée in the company of another man; Will tries to teach Karen how to drive.
Grace advises Will to play hard to get with his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale); Jack and Karen despair after learning their favorite TV series will be going off the air.
Will introduces his new boyfriend (Bobby Cannavale) to overly critical Grace; Karen tells Jack that their friendship will change after her wedding.
At Tina's (Lesley Ann Warren) urging, Will tries to find out if there is a new woman in his father's life; Jack's son decides to try out for the high-school cheerleading squad.
On the eve of his graduation from nursing school, Jack turns to Will for help writing his commencement address.
Karen moves her wedding to Las Vegas, where Jennifer Lopez agrees to sing at the ceremony.
Karen recruits Jack to help her get Jennifer Lopez to listen to Karen's new song; Grace takes out her frustration over her cheating husband on Will.
Jack wangles his way into Janet Jackson's (guest starring as herself) performance tour as a backup dancer.
As she attempts to steal doughnuts at an AA meeting, Grace has a surprise reunion with Val (Molly Shannon); Will and Jack attend a gay television focus group meeting.
Grace accuses Will of being too nice to strangers; Jack has trouble at his new company when his co-workers mock him about his Cher doll.
Despite the fact that Will has never had a happy birthday, his new relationship with Vince (Bobby Cannavale) gives him hope that this one will be.
Will convinces Jack to aid a local gay-bookstore owner to save his store from closing.
Will and Grace decide to invite Vince and Nadine (Kristin Davis) over, but they quickly learn that, despite similarities in friendship, they are polar opposites.
After a great date with someone else, Grace comes home to a garbled message from Leo; Karen and Jack try to set each other up, but things go awry.
Will, Grace, Jack and Karen go on a road trip for Grace's getaway weekend, but Jack and Karen hate the car ride and bail on the plan.

Vince's mother cannot make her traditional holiday feast, so Will volunteers to make a special meal, but Vince's mother refuses to give him any credit; Jack gives Vince's sister (Jamie-Lynn DiScala) pointers on keeping secrets.
When Ms. Simpson injures her back, a substitute teacher named Tony Crane takes over her class at Bayside; when all the girls fall for Mr. Crane, Zack and Slater become jealous.
When Kelly is nominated as homecoming queen, her dream is shattered as she faces the prospect of winning after she gets a zit; Zack comes up with a solution, but it does not unfold as he plans.
Zack bets against a Valley wrestler named Marvin Nedick that Slater will win his wrestling match against Nedick; things go wrong when Slater decides to quit wrestling.
In order for Kelly to go to a George Michael concert, she has to pass her science test. Zack persuades Screech to tutor Kelly, a ploy which is more for his benefit than for Kelly's.
Zack and his friends form a company selling friendship bracelets for a business class project. He names himself as boss, but Kelly, Jessie, and Slater feel he is treating them poorly.
Everyone is put into pairs for a class assignment to act out married life, so they can be prepared for marriage as adults.
Jessie and Zack (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar) run for student president, each for different reasons.
Zack's use of a subliminal tape to get Kelly to fall for him has results he never intended.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) schemes to get Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to be his girl land him in detention with a rival for her affections.
The pranks between rival schools Bayside and Valley escalate during the week of the city cheerleading finals.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) alien disguise is so believable it attracts a government UFO investigator.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) decides to throw a surprise birthday party for Screech (Dustin Diamond) in the principal's office.
Slater's (Mario Lopez) pet dies while in Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) care.
Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) chooses to go to the prom with Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar); Lisa and Screech (Lark Voorhies, Dustin Diamond) have a "trial" date.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes a leader of men when he joins a cadet corps to get out of detention.
The gang uses an old radio station in the school basement to hold a marathon. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's antics get Slater thrown out of driver education classes.
Screech's (Dustin Diamond) house party turns into a disaster when his mother's favorite statue is broken. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to cope when he ends up with two dates for the same night; Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) agrees to a blind date.
Zack has a waiter impersonate his father for a meeting with the principal.
The Miss Bayside Beauty Pageant attracts unusual contestants; Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) make a bet.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) becomes addicted to caffeine pills as she strives to be a perfect student. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) "Girls of Bayside" calendar catches the eye of a fashion photographer. With Dustin Diamond.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) advice line backfires and gets him into trouble with everyone. With Mario Lopez.

Zack makes a surprising discovery about his Native American heritage; Lisa learns her family tree includes a Black American hero of the Underground Railroad; Jessie grapples with guilt over her slave-trading ancestry.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) asks Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to go steady and then falls in love with the school nurse.
Mr. Belding's brother Rod (guest star Edward Blatchford) scores points with the class as a substitute history teacher. With Dennis Haskins and Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) plots to reunite Slater (Mario Lopez), Mr. Belding (Dennis Haskins) and himself with their feuding sweethearts.
Some underhanded shenanigans are employed to win a glee club competition.
A costume ball sets the stage for Zack and Kelly (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) to examine their relationship.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) has a hard time dealing with the fact that Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen) has a new boyfriend.
A minor accident sends Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) to the hospital, where he nervously faces the prospect of surgery.
Panic hits when Screech (Dustin Diamond) finds out he has to play a Russian exchange student in the chess finals. With Dennis Haskins.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) tries to impress a college girl by lying about his age.
The students adopt a new mascot when a stray ball injures a duck in the pond behind the football field.
Jessie's stepbrother Eric arrives from New York and blackmails her, Zack and Slater (Elizabeth Berkley, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez).
Eric tries to blackmail Slater (Mario Lopez) and learns a disturbing truth about his date with Lisa (Lark Voorhies).
The student council decides to hold a dance-date auction to raise money for new cheerleading uniforms.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) needs a high SAT score to achieve her dream of attending prestigious Stansbury University.
When a girl isn't allowed to try out for the wrestling team, the students band together and protest the decision.
Teenage movie star Johnny Dakota chooses Bayside as the site for an anti-drug commercial. With Mario Lopez and Dustin Diamond.
On Bayside's annual "cut school day," Mr. Belding warns Zack that if he is absent one more time he will be suspended.
Lisa and Screech make a "love machine" for their science project.
Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) latest moneymaking scheme involves a "Girls of Bayside" video-dating tape.
Jessie (Elizabeth Berkley) does everything in her power to break up her father's wedding. With Dustin Diamond.
Everyone gets summer jobs at a fancy beach club and decides to hold Zack's birthday party there.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) promises Mr. Carosi (Ernie Sabella) the gang will win a volleyball game against a rival beach club.
Stacy (Leah Remini) gets confused after she enters a contest at Zack's (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) urging and finds that he voted for Kelly (Tiffani-Amber Thiessen).
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is in love with Stacy (Leah Remini) but fears she is only interested in her college boyfriend.
Stacy (Leah Remini), in charge of the club for the day, learns her father booked two parties for the same night. With Mario Lopez.
Stacy (Leah Remini) moves out after her father forbids her to see Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar).
The entire gang goes to the mall to obtain U2 tickets and ends up camping out overnight. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
Jessie's father invites everyone to his Palm Springs resort to attend his wedding. With Elizabeth Berkley and Mario Lopez.
Casey Kasem (guest starring as himself) chronicles the rise of the rock group Zack Attack. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar.
The students are shocked during the Christmas season to discover the new girl working in Mr. Moody's store is homeless.
Zack's family invites Laura and her father home for Christmas.

Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) come to blows when they both fall for the new girl in their senior class.

Valentine's Day finds the gang at the Max reminiscing about past relationships. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Dustin Diamond.
Zack's plan to encourage the teachers to strike backfires on the students when the Academic Bowl is canceled.
The gang scrambles for dates as the senior prom approaches. With Mark-Paul Gosselaar and Mario Lopez.
A look into the future finds Belding with six students who are very similar to the gang from the class of 1993.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) is desperate enough to try ballet class when he learns he needs one more credit to graduate.
Zack's partner for a school project is the new girl at Bayside, a tough biker who is not at all impressed with him.
Zack (Mark-Paul Gosselaar) becomes overprotective of the physically challenged girl he is counseling on the teen line.
Zack and Slater (Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Mario Lopez) bet to see who can kiss Tori (Leanna Creel) first.
Zack tries to sneak out of detention so he can participate in a contest that has a trip to Hawaii as the prize.
Slater, Lisa, Zack and Screech (Mario Lopez, Lark Voorhies, Mark-Paul Gosselaar, Dustin Diamond) are involved in a drunken driving accident.

Freddie, Chris and Paddy confront the male midlife crisis by buying the perfect sports cars for "gentlemen of a certain age;" back at the track, Chris tests out the raucous new Toyota GR Yaris hot hatch.
Team Top Gear is up against the Florida locals in events including donk-car drag racing, a swamp buggy shoot-out, all ending up at the Freedom Factory Raceway for a NASCAR-style showdown.
On a mission to give the trundling trailblazer Sinclair one more eccentric adventure, Fred attempts to break the national speed limit whilst piloting the C5 down an Olympic bobsleigh run.
